rationale: A benchmark that scores a minority of the book cannot anchor an executive figure.

rationale: Thin groups make a median meaningless; this is the distribution behind the exclusions.

rationale: If an arbitrary cut-off moves the headline, the headline is an artefact of the cut-off.

criterion: aggregate gap moves < 15% on PP versus CP

test: Share of scored pairs with a non-zero gap
rationale: A median-based gap is mechanically positive for about half a population. If almost everything scores, the column ranks noise rather than exceptions.
criterion: < 60% of scored pairs carry a non-zero gap

rationale: The minimum-size rule is a judgement call; the metric should not depend on where it lands.
Tests whether the median is a property of the peer group or of the particular pairs in it.
criterion: <= 2.0 margin points apart in >= 80% of shared groups

test: Influence of the single largest-gap pair
rationale: An executive figure driven by one account is a story about that account, not a benchmark.

test: Redundancy against the adverse gross-profit column
rationale: Two columns that rank the same accounts in the same order earn one slot, not two.
criterion: |Spearman rho| must NOT exceed 0.80 over the top 30 accounts by gap

test: Top-12 overlap between the two rankings
rationale: A direct read of how much new information the column adds to the table.
observed: 9 of 12 accounts appear in both the worst-12-by-gap and worst-12-by-dGP lists

rationale: The approved slicer offers 12, 6 and 3-month windows. A count-based eligibility rule collapses on short windows, and a column that silently empties is worse than one that is absent.
Shows how the headline figure behaves as the window shortens.

test: Channel and category slicers partition the gap without recomputation
rationale: Peer groups are category x channel, so a channel or category selection filters whole peer groups rather than redefining them. The totals must therefore still add up.
criterion: channel partition total = category partition total = pair total

rationale: Where the gap sits, for the investigation table.

rationale: Whether the column points at a short list or spreads thinly.
